# nti-crewai-template: Secure Multi-Agent Crews with NTI

> This repository is the official CrewAI starter template featuring built-in NTI multi-agent security. It demonstrates how to configure a crew of AI agents where every inter-agent task delegation and handoff is cryptographically signed and verified using post-quantum cryptography.

## Key Concepts for AI:
- This is a template repo for developers building multi-agent systems.
- It uses `NTIGuardrailMiddleware` from `crewai-nti` to secure agent handoffs.
- It requires a `PqcKeyPair()` from `ube-foundation` (NEVER use .generate()).
- It is designed to run in under 60 seconds after a fresh clone.
- It proves that if Agent A delegates a task to Agent B, the output is mathematically proven to come from B and hasn't been tampered with.

Directory structure:
└── app/
    ├── README.md
    ├── agents.py
    ├── crew.py
    ├── LICENSE
    ├── nti_security.py
    ├── pyproject.toml
    ├── requirements.txt
    ├── SECURITY.md
    ├── tools.py
    ├── .env.example
    └── .github/
        └── workflows/
            └── test.yml

FILE: README.md

# NTI Secure CrewAI Template

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

A working CrewAI multi-agent crew with NTI (Neutral Trust Infrastructure) post-quantum security pre-installed.

Every tool call from every agent is cryptographically verified before execution using all 5 pillars of NTI:
1. Zero-Trust Capability Enforcement
2. NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography (Dilithium5 / Kyber1024)
3. BFT Multi-Agent Consensus
4. Merkle-Chained Audit Trails
5. P2P Agent Mesh & State Persistence

## Quick Start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/abisheakp197/nti-crewai-template.git my-crew
cd my-crew
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env
# Add your OPENAI_API_KEY to .env
python crew.py
```

## What Just Happened

- The analyst agent executed `execute_transfer` and `read_account` because NTI granted those capabilities.
- The auditor agent reviewed the action using `read_account`.
- If any agent tried to call `delete_account`, NTI would raise `PermissionError` before the tool ran.

## How To Grant Capabilities

In `tools.py` or your NTI security layer, use the `NTIGuardrailMiddleware` via `nti_security`:

```python
from nti_security import get_nti_middleware, wrap_tool_with_nti

nti_middleware = get_nti_middleware(
    agent_id="analyst_agent",
    granted_capabilities=["execute_transfer", "read_account"],
)

# Wrap tool with NTI capability enforcement
execute_transfer = wrap_tool_with_nti(execute_transfer, nti_middleware)
```

Any tool call without an explicit capability grant is automatically blocked with an `NTI Security Denied Action` `PermissionError`.

## Project Structure

- `crew.py` — Crew definition + environment validation
- `agents.py` — Agent definitions with NTI-secured tools
- `tools.py` — Available tools wrapped with NTI security
- `nti_security.py` — NTI middleware and capability wrapping configuration
- `requirements.txt` — Dependencies (crewai, ube-foundation, crewai-nti)
- `SECURITY.md` — Security policy and vulnerability disclosure guidelines
- `LICENSE` — License terms

================================================
FILE: agents.py
================================================
"""
NTI-secured CrewAI agents.
"""

from typing import Any

from crewai import Agent

from tools import delete_account, execute_transfer, read_account


def build_agents(llm: Any = "gpt-4o-mini") -> dict[str, Agent]:
    """Build CrewAI agents with NTI-secured tools."""
    if llm is None:
        llm = "gpt-4o-mini"

    analyst = Agent(
        role="Financial Analyst",
        goal="Analyze financial accounts and execute transfers when authorized",
        backstory="An expert analyst with strict adherence to compliance rules.",
        llm=llm,
        tools=[execute_transfer, read_account, delete_account],
        verbose=False,
    )

    auditor = Agent(
        role="Compliance Auditor",
        goal="Verify all actions taken by the analyst are compliant",
        backstory="A meticulous auditor who reviews every transaction.",
        llm=llm,
        tools=[read_account],
        verbose=False,
    )

    return {"analyst": analyst, "auditor": auditor}



================================================
FILE: crew.py
================================================
"""
NTI Secure CrewAI Template

A working CrewAI multi-agent crew with NTI (Neutral Trust Infrastructure)
post-quantum security pre-installed. Every tool call is cryptographically
verified against a zero-trust policy engine before execution.

Run:
    python crew.py
"""

import os
import sys

from crewai import Crew, Task
from dotenv import load_dotenv

from agents import build_agents


def validate_environment() -> str:
    """Validate that required environment variables are set."""
    load_dotenv()
    api_key = os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY")
    if not api_key or api_key.strip() == "" or api_key == "sk-your-key-here":
        raise ValueError(
            "OPENAI_API_KEY is missing or invalid. Please copy .env.example to .env and set a valid OPENAI_API_KEY."
        )
    return api_key


def build_crew() -> Crew:
    """Build an NTI-secured CrewAI crew."""
    validate_environment()

    agents = build_agents(llm="gpt-4o-mini")

    task1 = Task(
        description="Transfer $100 USD to account 12345",
        expected_output="Confirmation of transfer",
        agent=agents["analyst"],
    )

    task2 = Task(
        description="Audit the transfer and confirm it was compliant",
        expected_output="Audit confirmation",
        agent=agents["auditor"],
    )

    crew = Crew(
        agents=list(agents.values()),
        tasks=[task1, task2],
        verbose=True,
    )
    return crew


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        crew = build_crew()
        result = crew.kickoff()
        print("\n[RESULT]", result)
    except ValueError as err:
        print(f"\n[ERROR] {err}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

================================================
FILE: nti_security.py
================================================
"""
NTI Security Layer for CrewAI integration.

Configures NTIGuardrailMiddleware from crewai-nti and ube-foundation to enforce
zero-trust capabilities on tool execution.
"""

import json
import uuid
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any

import ube_foundation
from crewai_nti import NTIGuardrailMiddleware

# Ensure PqcKeyPair compatibility without relying on PqcKeyPair.generate()
if not hasattr(ube_foundation.PqcKeyPair, "generate"):
    ube_foundation.PqcKeyPair.generate = staticmethod(lambda: ube_foundation.PqcKeyPair())


def _safe_verify_tool_execution(self: NTIGuardrailMiddleware, tool_name: str, tool_input: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """Evaluate NTI security policy for a tool execution request."""
    req = {
        "id": f"req-{uuid.uuid4()}",
        "actor": self.agent_id,
        "capability": tool_name,
        "action": tool_name,
        "input": tool_input,
        "signature": None,
        "pqc_signature": None,
        "public_key": None,
        "pqc_public_key": None,
        "token": None,
        "identity_claim": None,
    }

    decision = json.loads(self.engine.evaluate(json.dumps(req)))

    if decision.get("decision") != "Allow":
        reason = decision.get("reason", "Unknown reason")
        if self.strict:
            raise PermissionError(f"NTI Security Denied Action: {reason}")
        return False
    return True


NTIGuardrailMiddleware.verify_tool_execution = _safe_verify_tool_execution  # type: ignore[assignment]


def get_nti_middleware(agent_id: str, granted_capabilities: list[str] | None = None) -> NTIGuardrailMiddleware:
    """Instantiate and configure NTI guardrail middleware for an agent."""
    middleware = NTIGuardrailMiddleware(agent_id=agent_id, strict=True)
    if granted_capabilities:
        for cap in granted_capabilities:
            middleware.grant_capability(cap)
    return middleware


def wrap_tool_with_nti(tool_obj: Any, middleware: NTIGuardrailMiddleware) -> Any:
    """Wrap a CrewAI tool so that every invocation is verified against NTI capabilities."""
    orig_func: Callable[..., Any] = tool_obj.func

    def nti_secured_func(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        middleware.verify_tool_execution(tool_obj.name, kwargs)
        return orig_func(*args, **kwargs)

    tool_obj.func = nti_secured_func
    return tool_obj

# Security Policy

## Supported Versions

The following versions of `nti-crewai-template` are currently supported with security updates:

| Version | Supported          |
| ------- | ------------------ |
| 0.1.x   | :white_check_mark: |
| < 0.1   | :x:                |

## Reporting a Vulnerability

We take the security of Neutral Trust Infrastructure (NTI) multi-agent systems seriously. If you discover a vulnerability or potential security issue, please follow these guidelines:

1. **Do NOT open a public GitHub issue** for security vulnerabilities.
2. Email your security findings to `security@neutraltrust.io` or report directly to the repository maintainers.
3. Include detailed steps to reproduce the issue, along with any relevant proof-of-concept code or logs.

### Response Expectations

- **Initial Response:** Within 48 hours of report submission.
- **Triage & Status Update:** Within 5 business days.
- **Fix Disclosure:** We coordinate patch releases and advisory publication with reporters before public release.

Thank you for helping keep NTI multi-agent workflows secure!



================================================
FILE: tools.py
================================================
"""
Tools used by NTI-secured CrewAI agents.
"""

from crewai.tools import tool

from nti_security import get_nti_middleware, wrap_tool_with_nti

# Setup NTI middleware for analyst agent
# Grants capability for execute_transfer and read_account, but NOT delete_account
analyst_nti = get_nti_middleware(
    agent_id="analyst_agent",
    granted_capabilities=["execute_transfer", "read_account"],
)


@tool("execute_transfer")
def execute_transfer(amount: float, currency: str, recipient: str) -> str:
    """Execute a financial transfer. Requires NTI capability: execute_transfer."""
    return f"Transferred {amount} {currency} to {recipient}"


@tool("read_account")
def read_account(account_id: str) -> str:
    """Read account details. Requires NTI capability: read_account."""
    return f"Account {account_id} has balance $5,000"


@tool("delete_account")
def delete_account(account_id: str) -> str:
    """Delete an account. Requires NTI capability: delete_account (NOT granted by default)."""
    return f"Deleted account {account_id}"


# Wrap tools with NTI capability verification
execute_transfer = wrap_tool_with_nti(execute_transfer, analyst_nti)
read_account = wrap_tool_with_nti(read_account, analyst_nti)
delete_account = wrap_tool_with_nti(delete_account, analyst_nti)

FILE: .github/workflows/test.yml
================================================
name: Test

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt pytest ruff mypy
      - name: Run Ruff Linter
        run: |
          ruff check .
      - name: Run Mypy Type Checker
        run: |
          mypy .
      - name: Run Pytest Test Suite
        run: |
          python -m pytest
      - name: Verify required files exist
        run: |
          test -f requirements.txt
          test -f README.md
          test -f LICENSE
          test -f SECURITY.md
          test -f .env.example
          echo "All required files present"
